summary: First sweep, structured sources only. The best finds are Germany-only, fully remote tech-lead roles on TypeScript/React: Recare (AI agent frontend for hospital discharge, 10) and CEEZER (carbon-credit platform, 9). Planhof's founding/lead engineer (EUR 90-105k), Modash's Vue 3/TypeScript product engineer and Seeq's JVM+React staff role score 8 each, though Seeq lists only the US. The ai-eng lane is thin at its honest edge: Langfuse fails only on Berlin travel, AiMi on level and Sourcegraph's agentic role on model training; no freelance posting reached 7, and FastRocket's 100% remote Java/Angular role (first posted 1 July) was dropped as stale although it is open until 29 September. Unknown stack or domain was scored 1, so unopened rows mostly land in kept; Remotive now holds 17 jobs and ignores its filters, Arbeitnow mixes in UK/FR/CH postings and Himalayas returns no cursor; vocab.json unchanged. Corrected after the run, on 2026-09-28, when shortlisting was tied to verified Germany eligibility: Seeq full-stack (US only) moved from shortlisted to dropped as not-germany, Seeq backend (not opened) from shortlisted to kept.
open_questions: Travel ceiling: Langfuse (open-source LLM observability, EUR 90-160k) asks for about a week in Berlin every two months, roughly 7 days a quarter. Acceptable? It is the closest ai-eng match so far.

Mid-level roles with a near-exact stack match (AiMi: React/TypeScript, Node, Lambda, DynamoDB, Cognito, Claude-driven development) were dropped as too-junior. Keep dropping them, or keep them when the stack fits this closely?
Seeq lists only the US on its ads but says pay is 'adjusted for other countries'. It was shortlisted as 'ask first'. Should a US-only location list count as not-germany instead?
Lead roles built on a stack the CV lacks (Rails at AREO, Go at vCluster) were dropped as stack-mismatch although the rubric alone would reach 7. Agree with that?
FastRocket's 100% remote Java/Angular role (Germany, permanent) closes on 2026-09-29. It was dropped as stale because it was first posted on 2026-07-01. Want it anyway?
Minimum salary (permanent) and minimum day rate (freelance): record them, or keep them as 'asked, not stored'?
Notice period at msg: when could a new role start?
Consultancies as a permanent employer: the default (down-rank) was applied to PAGNOS, QAVION, EggAI, ALTEN, nterra and virtual7. Keep it?
Italian-market roles: ShopFully (Italian, hires AI engineers in AT/DE/IT/ES) came up at mid level. Should Italian employers or Italian as a requirement get a boost?
Companies or industries to avoid, and a preferred company size (startup, scale-up, established)?

sources.name: arbeitnow
sources.note: 326 + 325 rows, 23 with remote:true; only remote rows with lane titles recorded. The feed now mixes arbeitnow.co.uk/.fr/.ch postings (UK, France, Switzerland) into the German one.

sources.name: himalayas
sources.note: 20 rows per query (totals 258, 70, 628, 118, 0); the search endpoint returns no nextCursor despite the API comment, so page 1 only. Re-queried once to read country lists. Employer-posted jobs are hosted on Himalayas itself, so its job page is the posting.

sources.name: remotive
sources.note: Free API holds 17 jobs in total and ignores category and search: both queries returned the same 17 rows. Asks for at most 4 calls a day.

sources.name: remoteok
sources.note: tag=java returns mostly non-tech rows carrying unrelated tags, so the tag filter is unreliable; the untagged feed has 99 jobs (2026-07-31 to 09-26), most without a usable location. Filtered titles locally.

sources.name: weworkremotely
sources.note: 41 + 5 items. The region field says 'Anywhere in the World' even when the country field is US-only; trust the country field. Posting pages return 403 to WebFetch, so WWR rows stay unverified.

sources.name: germantechjobs
sources.note: No location field; 54 lane titles, of which only those whose feed text states a remote or onsite policy were recorded. Most lane roles say nothing about remote.

sources.name: hn-whoishiring
